topic: Requirements to executable specifications and code generation

components.title: Deconstructing Requirements into Public Method Contracts
components.teaches: Students will learn how to analyze informal requirements to identify public module methods, parameter contracts, and class invariants. They will establish strict preconditions, postconditions, and interface signatures needed before writing formal specifications.

components.title: Structuring Executable Specifications in Spec-Driven Frameworks
components.teaches: Students will learn the concrete syntax and structural conventions of spec-driven frameworks such as pytest-bdd or Behave. They will map high-level requirement statements into executable Given-When-Then scenario definitions tied directly to public API hooks.

components.title: Step-by-Step Translation of Requirements to Executable Specs
components.teaches: Students will follow a complete worked example translating a payment-processing requirement brief into an automated executable specification suite. They will observe how each requirement constraint is systematically formalized into assertion-backed test harnesses that cover all public methods.

components.title: Prompt Patterns for Generating Executable Specifications
components.teaches: Students will learn effective prompting architectures to instruct LLMs to synthesize spec-driven test suites from unstructured requirements documents. They will configure system instructions and interface schema definitions to eliminate hallucinations in method signatures and types.

components.title: Hands-on Authoring of Executable Specs from Requirements
components.teaches: Students will work in pairs to translate a natural-language requirement specification for a user session manager into an executable specification suite using a BDD framework. They will execute their specs against stub interfaces to confirm that every required public method is bounded by executable assertions.
